pathway.title: QXO, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage after the TopBuild closing is not established, and the pre-closing ratios are a floor rather than a measure. Net debt was USD 3,266 million at 30 June 2026, USD 6,266 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan drawn on 1 July 2026, and USD 3,289 million after the USD 23 million Convertible Preferred dividend paid after the quarter end; net leverage was 4.51x adjusted and 9.45x reported EBITDA, and pro forma net leverage is not established. The ratios exclude TopBuild's earnings, cash and debt and count USD 3,000 million of escrowed notes as debt without their cash, so they cannot show where leverage lands once combined results are reported. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-01

Fixed charges at the new debt level exceed what the pre-TopBuild earnings can carry, so the credit rests on TopBuild's contribution. Coupons on the debt outstanding at 30 June 2026 run at about USD 401 million a year against cash interest paid of USD 221.0 million, and at about USD 570 million with the incremental term loan at the existing term loan rate, which is an assumption because its margin is not stated. Adding about USD 264 million of preferred dividends gives about USD 834 million, or 0.87x of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA; adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,140 million would be needed for 2.00x cover of interest alone, about USD 416 million more than the pre-TopBuild base. About 42.38% of principal is floating after the incremental loan, and a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 39 million of interest a year; Series C dividends of USD 142.5 million can be paid in shares, which is the main cash lever. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-08; calculation C-09; calculation C-10; calculation C-11; calculation C-12; calculation C-13

Earnings quality is the second constraint, because more than half of adjusted EBITDA is add-backs. Add-backs were USD 379.1 million of USD 724.8 million of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, 52.30%, and USD 514.1 million against reported EBITDA of USD 133.7 million in FY2025; transaction costs of USD 52 million and transformation costs of USD 24 million were added back in the second quarter of 2026 alone. The company defines the adjustments itself, so reported EBITDA of USD 345.7 million is the conservative base; stock-based compensation is the one recurring item, and the other five add-backs, 71.90% of the FY2025 total, follow the acquisitions and should shrink as integration ends. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 10; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-02

The trading trend is weaker than the reported sales growth suggests. Excluding Kodiak, net sales were 1.56% below the company's pro forma prior year in the second quarter of 2026 and 5.05% below in the first half; adjusted gross margin fell by 0.6 percentage points in the quarter and 1.0 percentage points in the half, because product cost rose faster than selling prices; and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.38% against 10.70% a year earlier. The chief executive says the second-quarter result reflects current market conditions; volume and price effects are not separated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C-04; calculation C-06; calculation C-07

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Total liquidity, unrestricted cash plus ABL availability, was USD 4,704 million at 30 June 2026, a balance after the closing that is not established; no principal falls due before 2030 and USD 9,100 million falls due between 2031 and 2034; and the springing fixed charge test on the ABL is not in force because availability is at least 9.65x the highest level at which it could apply. Replaying a seasonal half year at run-rate interest and preferred dividends would use about USD 511 million, covered 9.20x by that liquidity, so near-term distress is unlikely even before TopBuild's cash flow is counted, and the company states that liquidity is sufficient for the next 12 months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-18

Cash generation is thin and seasonal. Free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months, 19.48% of adjusted EBITDA, before acquisitions and preferred dividends; operating cash flow was negative in the first half of 2026 as working capital absorbed cash; and 41.65% of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA came in the third quarter of 2025 against 0.17% in the first quarter of 2026. A single quarter should not be annualised, and the first quarter of 2027 is the first seasonal low with the new interest and preferred dividends in place. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-03; calculation C-05

Demand is defensive and customer risk is low, but supplier concentration and cost pass-through limit margin protection. The company states that about 80% of industry revenue is repair and re-roofing and that no customer exceeded 1% of 2025 net sales, and it says many expenses are fixed in a downturn; three suppliers each supplied at least 10% of 2025 purchases and nearly 35% in total, which corrects an earlier statement in Business & governance that supplier shares were not supplied. Asphalt and steel-linked prices are volatile, increases are usually but not always passed on in time, and a change in vendor rebates would lower gross margin. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-22; calculation C-26

Financial policy supports creditors less than the equity funding history suggests. Kodiak and most of Beacon were funded with equity, preferred stock and cash, but the filings state no leverage target, TopBuild was funded with USD 6,000 million of new debt, 40.00% of the price, and USD 4,575 million of preferred stock carries cash dividends ahead of common equity; control is concentrated and the investors' shares are stated only as of the annual report. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-24; calculation C-27

cells.text: Largest publicly traded distributor of roofing, waterproofing and complementary building products in North America; serves all 50 US states and seven Canadian provinces
About 600 branches at 2025-12-31, about 96% in the US and about 97% leased; 7,794 active employees; more than 110,000 customers

Distribution of manufacturers' products to contractors, builders and retailers; second-quarter 2026 net sales by line: residential roofing 39.0%, non-residential roofing 22.7%, complementary building products 37.9%, software 0.4%
Professional contractors, home builders, building owners, lumberyards and retailers; no single customer above 1% of 2025 net sales

Manufacturers of roofing, complementary and waterproofing products; the largest named include Owens Corning, GAF, Carlisle Construction Materials, CertainTeed, IKO, TAMKO, Johns Manville, James Hardie, Dow and Sika; no purchase shares are given
Net sales and net income expected highest in the quarters ending June 30, September 30 and December 31; low profit or losses in the quarter ending March 31

Gross margin 24.7% in the second quarter of 2026 against 21.1% a year earlier, when USD 80 million of inventory fair value adjustment weighed on margin; selling, general and administrative expense 20.0% of net sales against 24.0%

Target of USD 50 billion of annual revenue within the next decade through acquisitions and organic growth; the annual report says the company is actively involved in processes for potential acquisitions

Plan to more than double EBITDA by 2030 and to reach USD 50 billion of annual revenue within the decade; the fourth-quarter release says the EBITDA run rate with Kodiak exceeds USD 1 billion; no base year or definition of EBITDA is given for either statement

North America's largest distributor and installer of insulation, second-largest distributor of roofing products, second-largest publicly traded distributor of lumber and building materials and largest distributor of waterproofing products, as stated after the TopBuild closing

runs.text: Liquidity and maturities give the structure time. Total liquidity of USD 4,704 million at 30 June 2026 covers a replayed seasonal half year at run-rate charges 9.20x, no principal falls due before 2030, and the springing ABL test is not in force, so a weak season would be absorbed before any covenant or refinancing pressure arises. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-18

Demand is defensive and diversified across customers. About 80% of industry revenue is repair and re-roofing, no customer exceeded 1% of 2025 net sales and complementary products reached 37.9% of second-quarter 2026 net sales, so revenue depends on a large number of small contractors and on need-driven repairs rather than on a few accounts or on new construction alone. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C-25; calculation C-26

Equity and preferred investors have funded the larger deals. New debt was 42.28% of the Beacon price and 40.00% of the TopBuild price, and Kodiak used none, so equity and preferred stock sit beneath the debt, although the USD 4,575 million of preferred stock carries cash dividends. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-24

Market access appears intact. At 30 June 2026 the 2031, 2032 and 2034 notes carried fair values of 102.13%, 103.38% and 102.87% of principal, including the notes issued two weeks earlier, so investors priced the debt above par before the closing; this is one pricing point, not a quotation history, and it predates the closing and the TopBuild debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C-30

Capital intensity is low. Capital expenditures were 1.14% of FY2025 net sales, so cash flow depends on working capital and acquisitions rather than on heavy reinvestment, and capital expenditure offers little relief in a downturn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-05

Leverage after the TopBuild closing is not established and fixed charges are large. Run-rate interest of about USD 570 million and preferred dividends of about USD 264 million total about USD 834 million, 0.87x of pre-TopBuild adjusted EBITDA, so the combined business must earn well above the earnings base supplied to carry the structure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-09; calculation C-12

Earnings quality is weak. Add-backs are 52.30% of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA and reported EBITDA is USD 345.7 million against adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million, so coverage and leverage depend on the issuer's own definitions. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-02

The trading trend is negative. Organic net sales were 1.56% below the pro forma prior year in the second quarter of 2026 and adjusted gross margin fell 0.6 percentage points, so volume and price are moving against earnings while many expenses are fixed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C-06; calculation C-07

Cash flow is seasonal and thin. Free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months and operating cash flow was negative in the first half of 2026, so preferred dividends and the first coupons on the new notes in January 2027 fall into the seasonal low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-05

Supply is concentrated. Three suppliers each supplied at least 10% of 2025 purchases and nearly 35% in total, and cost increases are not always passed on in time, so an allocation or price shock would reach margin quickly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C-22

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Beacon was the first acquisition and turned a software company into a building products distributor. It closed on 29 April 2025 for a net purchase price of USD 10,644 million, made up of USD 7,736 million for the shares, USD 104 million for converted equity awards and USD 2,948 million to repay Beacon's own debt, less USD 144 million of cash acquired. New debt at closing was USD 2,250 million of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and a USD 2,250 million term loan, with an asset-based facility of up to USD 2,000 million alongside; equity raised around the closing came from private placements and public offerings. Beacon was determined to be the predecessor for financial reporting, but the statements supplied show the company's own results before 29 April 2025, which exclude Beacon. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C-01

Two capital moves in 2025 reduced the debt taken for Beacon and its cost. A voluntary prepayment of USD 1,400 million on 29 May 2025, funded from the May equity and preferred offerings, left USD 850 million of term loan, and a repricing on 5 November 2025 cut the Term SOFR margin from 3.00% to 2.00%. On 27 May 2025 the company also issued 5.50% Series B Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock for USD 558 million net, a USD 575 million claim that must convert into common shares. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; calculation C-03; calculation C-04; calculation C-13

Kodiak, a distributor of lumber, trusses, windows and doors, construction supplies, waterproofing and roofing, closed on 1 April 2026 and was funded without new debt. The announced price was about USD 2.25 billion, but the closing-date table gives a net purchase price of USD 2,222 million: USD 478 million paid to sellers, USD 1,503 million to repay Kodiak's own debt and USD 257 million of company shares, less USD 16 million of cash acquired. Series C preferred stock of USD 2,000 million gross, issued to AP Quince Holdings, L.P., a fund managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc., and other investors, paid the cash cost with USD 28 million to spare. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C-05; calculation C-06; calculation C-07

TopBuild, the largest distributor and installer of insulation in North America, was signed on 18 April 2026 and closed on 1 July 2026, one day after the latest balance sheet. The filing for the first quarter gave a price of about USD 17.0 billion; the filing for the second quarter gives about USD 15 billion, made up of about USD 6.4 billion of cash and new company shares, and neither explains the USD 2,000 million difference. Closing was funded by USD 3,000 million released from escrow on the 2031 and 2034 notes, a USD 3,000 million incremental term loan due 1 July 2033 and USD 1,000 million of Series C preferred stock, so new debt was 40.00% of the price and the three sources exceed the stated cash consideration by about USD 600 million, which the filing attributes in general terms to related fees and expenses. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_qxo-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-03-31_qxo-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C-08; calculation C-09; calculation C-10; calculation C-22

The 2031 and 2034 notes of USD 1,500 million each were issued on 17 June 2026 into escrow, secured by the escrow until closing and unsecured with guarantees from the wholly owned domestic restricted subsidiaries after release. They are included in debt at 30 June 2026 although their cash was restricted, and the incremental term loan was drawn after that date, so no balance sheet in the documents shows both. The borrowing group's debt now consists of the ABL facility, the term loan including the incremental loan, the 2032 secured notes and the 2031 and 2034 unsecured notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 8; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The leverage picture turns on three choices the reader must make. Net debt of USD 3,266 million at 30 June 2026 is 9.45x reported EBITDA and 4.51x adjusted EBITDA, and USD 3,000 million of it is the escrowed notes counted as debt while the matching cash is restricted and outside the cash figure; with the escrow counted, net debt would be USD 266 million. Excluding the escrow, net debt rose from USD 12.3 million at 31 March 2026 to USD 266 million at 30 June 2026. The real step-up is the incremental term loan of USD 3,000 million drawn on 1 July 2026, which lifts standalone net debt to USD 6,266 million before any TopBuild earnings are counted, so creditors should treat the reported ratios as a floor on post-closing leverage, not a measure of it.

fields.value: Coverage is thin on reported earnings and adequate on adjusted earnings. Cash interest paid over the twelve months was USD 221.0 million, which covers reported EBITDA of USD 345.7 million 1.56x and adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million 3.28x. Cash interest is also a floor on what the debt will cost: the notes issued in June 2026 pay a first coupon in January 2027 and the incremental term loan was drawn on 1 July 2026, so neither is in the interest paid to date, while the earnings base excludes TopBuild. Cover on the enlarged company cannot be judged until the combined earnings are reported.

fields.value: Cash generation is seasonal and modest. Operating cash flow was negative in the first half of both years, USD 146 million outflow in 2026, because receivables and inventories absorb cash before the peak season; the twelve-month figure of USD 253.4 million less capital expenditures of USD 112.2 million leaves free cash flow of USD 141.2 million before acquisitions and preferred dividends. fields.value: Data-quality and definition risks are limited but real. The issuer prints no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from net income, taxes, net interest, depreciation and amortization; depreciation inside cost of products sold adds USD 2 million to the second-quarter and half-year figures; the 2026 second-quarter documents print whole millions while earlier ones print one decimal, which moves derived sums by up to USD 0.4 million; and the Kodiak price differs between the annual report and the later quarterly report. No supplier finance, factoring or customer deposits were found; deferred revenue sits inside accrued expenses and is not sized separately.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events are kept out of the period figures. The TopBuild closing on 1 July 2026 brought the incremental term loan, the release of the escrowed notes' cash, a further tranche of Series C preferred shares issued for USD 1.0 billion and new common shares issued to former TopBuild holders; a Convertible Preferred Stock dividend of USD 23 million was paid after the quarter end. The most material gap is the absence of any balance sheet or TopBuild statement after that date, which leaves post-closing net debt, leverage and interest cost not established beyond the standalone adjustments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO, Inc. (issuer id qxo), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, transactions and new debt issues, ownership and control, governance, sponsor and shareholder behaviour, capital allocation and issuer history from the supplied filings and releases, with the latest period ending 30 June 2026 and events to 1 July 2026. No credit recommendation, peer ranking or recovery view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO is a founder-controlled consolidator whose creditors are exposed to acquisition appetite rather than to extraction: preferred equity funded Kodiak, but new debt funded 40% of the roughly USD 15,000 million TopBuild purchase. Control sits with the founder, who held about 22.1% of the voting power, and his investment vehicle, which may designate 40% of the board. Preferred stock of USD 4,575 million at liquidation preference ranks ahead of common equity, and the three deals since April 2025 total about USD 27,866 million of price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated in one founder group, which supports continuity of the acquisition strategy and removes outside challenge to it. Brad Jacobs held about 22.1% of the voting power at the date of the annual report, and Jacobs Private Equity II, LLC may designate 40% of the board for as long as the investors in the 2024 equity deal keep at least 30% of fully diluted votes, a share the company put at 39.4% at that date. The board includes a lead independent director, but the independence of the other directors is not stated, and no later filing updates these figures after the 2026 share and Series C issuances, so the headroom above the 30% threshold is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition funding follows no fixed policy, so leverage tolerance has to be read deal by deal. Beacon used USD 4,500 million of new debt against a net price of USD 10,644 million, a share of 42.28%, and USD 1,400 million of that debt was repaid within a month from equity proceeds; Kodiak used no new debt; TopBuild used USD 6,000 million against a price of about USD 15,000 million, a share of 40.00%. None of the seven documents states a leverage target, a credit-rating objective or a deleveraging plan after TopBuild; management states a plan to more than double EBITDA by 2030, which is a growth goal without a base year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The preferred stack is the largest claim ahead of common equity and behind all debt, and its cash-pay features draw on the same cash as debt service. Liquidation preferences total USD 4,575 million. The Convertible Preferred pays 9%, which is USD 90.0 million a year, and Jacobs Private Equity II, LLC holds 90.00% of it; Series C pays 4.75%, which is USD 142.5 million a year at the full USD 3,000 million; and the Mandatory Convertible Preferred pays 5.50%. The company paid USD 84 million of preferred dividends in the first half of 2026, a half in which operating cash flow was negative. Series C is carried as mezzanine equity because holders can require cash redemption after a fundamental change, and a change of control would separately trigger a 101% repurchase offer on the notes, although the definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No extraction, related-party payment or creditor-adverse liability management is documented beyond the contractual preferred dividends, and that finding is limited to what the filings disclose. The only common dividend was USD 17.4 million in June 2024, before any acquisition, and the company says it does not intend to pay another; the only change to existing debt terms described, apart from the new incremental loan, is a cut in the term loan margin from 3.00% to 2.00%. The company calls the limits on restricted payments not significant given that policy, so creditors should not treat those limits as a binding check on distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is defensive in demand and seasonal in cash flow. The company states that about 80% of industry revenue is repair and re-roofing, no customer exceeded 1% of 2025 net sales, and the first quarter is expected to bring low profit or a loss. Complementary products reached 37.9% of second-quarter 2026 net sales, with Kodiak contributing USD 595 million of the total, against 22.4% in the second quarter of 2025, which held Beacon for only two months; supplier concentration is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is adequate for a listed filer but leaves gaps that matter to a creditor. The auditor's opinion on 2025 is unmodified with one critical audit matter on the valuation of Beacon's customer relationships; management excluded Beacon, which was 86.1% of consolidated assets and 99.1% of revenue, from its internal-control assessment as the rules allow for one year, so no auditor attestation on internal control exists; and the purchase price allocation for TopBuild is not yet available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is how the first two deals were funded. Debt remaining after the May 2025 prepayment covered 29.12% of the Beacon price, with the rest met from equity and cash; USD 1,450 million raised in May 2025 exceeded the USD 1,400 million prepayment; and Kodiak needed no new debt because Series C preferred stock covered its cash cost with USD 28 million to spare. The only cash flowing to the founder group in the filings is its contractual share of preferred dividends, USD 81.0 million a year, and the preferred investors hold instruments that rank behind every creditor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three developments would raise the risk assessment: a further acquisition funded mainly with debt, evidence that cash is moved from the borrowing group to the parent to pay preferred dividends outside the restricted-payment limits, or related-party arrangements and board-seat rights for the Series C investors that the supplied documents do not show. Three would lower it: a stated leverage target together with repayment of the incremental term loan, conversion of preferred stock into common shares, which would end the cash dividends but dilute control, and a proxy statement that discloses an independent board majority and no related-party payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The control conclusion rests on voting and designation percentages stated at the annual report date; if the 2026 issuances have taken the investors' fully diluted share below the 30% threshold, the founder group's board designation right would shrink and the concentration finding would weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The no-extraction finding covers only what the filings and notes disclose; the independence of most directors, related-party transactions, compensation and fees sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a related-party payment would not be visible and the finding could reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The finding that creditor protections are limited relies on the company's summaries of the debt and preferred documents; if the executed documents define permitted holders or restricted-payment baskets more tightly than summarised, the view that distributions are unchecked would soften.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - TopBuild is described only by its purchase terms, so the operating model and the funding conclusion cover the business before 1 July 2026; the stated price also differs between filings, which makes the 40% debt share an approximation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Beacon was the first acquisition and turned a software company into a building products distributor. It closed on 29 April 2025 for a net purchase price of USD 10,644 million, made up of USD 7,736 million for the shares, USD 104 million for converted equity awards and USD 2,948 million to repay Beacon's own debt, less USD 144 million of cash acquired. New debt at closing was USD 2,250 million of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and a USD 2,250 million term loan, with an asset-based facility of up to USD 2,000 million alongside; equity raised around the closing came from private placements and public offerings. Beacon was determined to be the predecessor for financial reporting, but the statements supplied show the company's own results before 29 April 2025, which exclude Beacon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two capital moves in 2025 reduced the debt taken for Beacon and its cost. A voluntary prepayment of USD 1,400 million on 29 May 2025, funded from the May equity and preferred offerings, left USD 850 million of term loan, and a repricing on 5 November 2025 cut the Term SOFR margin from 3.00% to 2.00%. On 27 May 2025 the company also issued 5.50% Series B Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock for USD 558 million net, a USD 575 million claim that must convert into common shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kodiak, a distributor of lumber, trusses, windows and doors, construction supplies, waterproofing and roofing, closed on 1 April 2026 and was funded without new debt. The announced price was about USD 2.25 billion, but the closing-date table gives a net purchase price of USD 2,222 million: USD 478 million paid to sellers, USD 1,503 million to repay Kodiak's own debt and USD 257 million of company shares, less USD 16 million of cash acquired. Series C preferred stock of USD 2,000 million gross, issued to AP Quince Holdings, L.P., a fund managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc., and other investors, paid the cash cost with USD 28 million to spare.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TopBuild, the largest distributor and installer of insulation in North America, was signed on 18 April 2026 and closed on 1 July 2026, one day after the latest balance sheet. The filing for the first quarter gave a price of about USD 17.0 billion; the filing for the second quarter gives about USD 15 billion, made up of about USD 6.4 billion of cash and new company shares, and neither explains the USD 2,000 million difference. Closing was funded by USD 3,000 million released from escrow on the 2031 and 2034 notes, a USD 3,000 million incremental term loan due 1 July 2033 and USD 1,000 million of Series C preferred stock, so new debt was 40.00% of the price and the three sources exceed the stated cash consideration by about USD 600 million, which the filing attributes in general terms to related fees and expenses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by concentrated founder control and an acquisition-led funding pattern, because large debt-funded deals and cash-pay preferred stock can raise leverage and fixed charges faster than earnings grow, which implies higher event and refinancing risk for creditors. Countervailing evidence is the equity and preferred funding of the first two deals, the absence of documented extraction and stated covenant compliance. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO, Inc. (issuer id qxo), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: fundamental credit view of business quality, cash flow, liquidity, leverage tolerance, refinancing capacity and the downside path, from the supplied filings and releases and the three earlier analyses, with the latest period ending 30 June 2026 and events to 1 July 2026. No security recommendation, legal conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO's fundamental credit is adequate before the TopBuild closing and cannot be fully assessed after it: liquidity and maturities are comfortable, but the leverage that matters rests on an acquired earnings base that no supplied document reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-01; calculation C-15; calculation C-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage at 30 June 2026 was 4.51x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 9.45x reported EBITDA, and pro forma net leverage after the incremental term loan is not established. Run-rate interest of about USD 570 million, assuming the new loan costs what the existing term loan does, and preferred dividends of about USD 264 million together exceed twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million, so TopBuild's earnings must carry the structure while organic sales are falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-01; calculation C-06; calculation C-09; calculation C-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage after the TopBuild closing is not established, and the pre-closing ratios are a floor rather than a measure. Net debt was USD 3,266 million at 30 June 2026, USD 6,266 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan drawn on 1 July 2026, and USD 3,289 million after the USD 23 million Convertible Preferred dividend paid after the quarter end; net leverage was 4.51x adjusted and 9.45x reported EBITDA, and pro forma net leverage is not established. The ratios exclude TopBuild's earnings, cash and debt and count USD 3,000 million of escrowed notes as debt without their cash, so they cannot show where leverage lands once combined results are reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fixed charges at the new debt level exceed what the pre-TopBuild earnings can carry, so the credit rests on TopBuild's contribution. Coupons on the debt outstanding at 30 June 2026 run at about USD 401 million a year against cash interest paid of USD 221.0 million, and at about USD 570 million with the incremental term loan at the existing term loan rate, which is an assumption because its margin is not stated. Adding about USD 264 million of preferred dividends gives about USD 834 million, or 0.87x of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA; adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,140 million would be needed for 2.00x cover of interest alone, about USD 416 million more than the pre-TopBuild base. About 42.38% of principal is floating after the incremental loan, and a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 39 million of interest a year; Series C dividends of USD 142.5 million can be paid in shares, which is the main cash lever.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 49; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-08; calculation C-09; calculation C-10; calculation C-11; calculation C-12; calculation C-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the second constraint, because more than half of adjusted EBITDA is add-backs. Add-backs were USD 379.1 million of USD 724.8 million of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, 52.30%, and USD 514.1 million against reported EBITDA of USD 133.7 million in FY2025; transaction costs of USD 52 million and transformation costs of USD 24 million were added back in the second quarter of 2026 alone. The company defines the adjustments itself, so reported EBITDA of USD 345.7 million is the conservative base; stock-based compensation is the one recurring item, and the other five add-backs, 71.90% of the FY2025 total, follow the acquisitions and should shrink as integration ends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 10; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trading trend is weaker than the reported sales growth suggests. Excluding Kodiak, net sales were 1.56% below the company's pro forma prior year in the second quarter of 2026 and 5.05% below in the first half; adjusted gross margin fell by 0.6 percentage points in the quarter and 1.0 percentage points in the half, because product cost rose faster than selling prices; and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 8.38% against 10.70% a year earlier. The chief executive says the second-quarter result reflects current market conditions; volume and price effects are not separated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C-04; calculation C-06; calculation C-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Total liquidity, unrestricted cash plus ABL availability, was USD 4,704 million at 30 June 2026, a balance after the closing that is not established; no principal falls due before 2030 and USD 9,100 million falls due between 2031 and 2034; and the springing fixed charge test on the ABL is not in force because availability is at least 9.65x the highest level at which it could apply. Replaying a seasonal half year at run-rate interest and preferred dividends would use about USD 511 million, covered 9.20x by that liquidity, so near-term distress is unlikely even before TopBuild's cash flow is counted, and the company states that liquidity is sufficient for the next 12 months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is thin and seasonal. Free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months, 19.48% of adjusted EBITDA, before acquisitions and preferred dividends; operating cash flow was negative in the first half of 2026 as working capital absorbed cash; and 41.65% of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA came in the third quarter of 2025 against 0.17% in the first quarter of 2026. A single quarter should not be annualised, and the first quarter of 2027 is the first seasonal low with the new interest and preferred dividends in place.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-03; calculation C-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is defensive and customer risk is low, but supplier concentration and cost pass-through limit margin protection. The company states that about 80% of industry revenue is repair and re-roofing and that no customer exceeded 1% of 2025 net sales, and it says many expenses are fixed in a downturn; three suppliers each supplied at least 10% of 2025 purchases and nearly 35% in total, which corrects an earlier statement in Business & governance that supplier shares were not supplied. Asphalt and steel-linked prices are volatile, increases are usually but not always passed on in time, and a change in vendor rebates would lower gross margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-22; calculation C-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy supports creditors less than the equity funding history suggests. Kodiak and most of Beacon were funded with equity, preferred stock and cash, but the filings state no leverage target, TopBuild was funded with USD 6,000 million of new debt, 40.00% of the price, and USD 4,575 million of preferred stock carries cash dividends ahead of common equity; control is concentrated and the investors' shares are stated only as of the annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-24; calculation C-27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the structure is funded and not close to any test. Liquidity covers a replayed seasonal outflow 9.20x, no principal is due before 2030, the ABL covenant is not in force, the first two deals were paid largely with equity, preferred stock and cash, and tangible assets of USD 12,052 million cover gross debt 2.00x; TopBuild also adds an earnings base that is in no ratio, so if its earnings are large against the USD 3,000 million of added debt, leverage could fall below the pre-closing 4.51x on adjusted EBITDA. Most of the add-backs are tied to the acquisitions and should fall as integration ends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-02; calculation C-14; calculation C-16; calculation C-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three developments would raise the risk assessment: a first combined report showing net leverage above the pre-closing level on adjusted EBITDA, organic sales still falling with adjusted gross margin below its second-quarter level, or ABL drawings to fund the first-quarter seasonal outflow. Three would lower it: combined results showing net leverage below the pre-closing level, a return to organic growth with stable gross margin, and cash dividends cut through share payment or early repayment of the incremental term loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No TopBuild earnings, cash or debt are supplied, so leverage and cover after the closing are bounds rather than measurements; if TopBuild's contribution is large against the added debt, the conclusion that fixed charges exceed the earnings base would reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The margin on the incremental term loan is not stated, so the interest estimate assumes the existing term loan rate; a higher margin would deepen the shortfall in cover and a lower one would narrow it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The organic sales trend rests on the company's unaudited pro forma net sales for Beacon, which do not separate volume from price; if that base is overstated, the decline would be smaller and the trading conclusion weaker.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, dated market quotes or peer set are supplied and the only market input is the fair value of the debt at 30 June 2026, so the comparison with other leveraged distributors is qualitative and the view of refinancing capacity rests on maturities, liquidity and that single pricing point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside figures repeat observed first-half 2026 trends on the pre-TopBuild base and pair them with post-closing charges; if the enlarged business behaves differently, the scenario outcome moves in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities give the structure time. Total liquidity of USD 4,704 million at 30 June 2026 covers a replayed seasonal half year at run-rate charges 9.20x, no principal falls due before 2030, and the springing ABL test is not in force, so a weak season would be absorbed before any covenant or refinancing pressure arises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is defensive and diversified across customers. About 80% of industry revenue is repair and re-roofing, no customer exceeded 1% of 2025 net sales and complementary products reached 37.9% of second-quarter 2026 net sales, so revenue depends on a large number of small contractors and on need-driven repairs rather than on a few accounts or on new construction alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C-25; calculation C-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity and preferred investors have funded the larger deals. New debt was 42.28% of the Beacon price and 40.00% of the TopBuild price, and Kodiak used none, so equity and preferred stock sit beneath the debt, although the USD 4,575 million of preferred stock carries cash dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Market access appears intact. At 30 June 2026 the 2031, 2032 and 2034 notes carried fair values of 102.13%, 103.38% and 102.87% of principal, including the notes issued two weeks earlier, so investors priced the debt above par before the closing; this is one pricing point, not a quotation history, and it predates the closing and the TopBuild debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low. Capital expenditures were 1.14% of FY2025 net sales, so cash flow depends on working capital and acquisitions rather than on heavy reinvestment, and capital expenditure offers little relief in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage after the TopBuild closing is not established and fixed charges are large. Run-rate interest of about USD 570 million and preferred dividends of about USD 264 million total about USD 834 million, 0.87x of pre-TopBuild adjusted EBITDA, so the combined business must earn well above the earnings base supplied to carry the structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-09; calculation C-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is weak. Add-backs are 52.30% of twelve-month adjusted EBITDA and reported EBITDA is USD 345.7 million against adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million, so coverage and leverage depend on the issuer's own definitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trading trend is negative. Organic net sales were 1.56% below the pro forma prior year in the second quarter of 2026 and adjusted gross margin fell 0.6 percentage points, so volume and price are moving against earnings while many expenses are fixed.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C-06; calculation C-07

fields.value: Cash flow is seasonal and thin. Free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months and operating cash flow was negative in the first half of 2026, so preferred dividends and the first coupons on the new notes in January 2027 fall into the seasonal low.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supply is concentrated. Three suppliers each supplied at least 10% of 2025 purchases and nearly 35% in total, and cost increases are not always passed on in time, so an allocation or price shock would reach margin quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: QXO is a distributor of roofing, waterproofing and complementary building products in North America that grew from a small software business through three acquisitions in 14 months. In the second quarter of 2026 residential roofing was 39.0% of net sales, non-residential roofing 22.7% and complementary products 37.9%, and TopBuild adds insulation distribution and installation from 1 July 2026, so the mix is moving away from roofing and dilutes the demand evidence the business has built up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is mostly repair and re-roofing, which the company puts at about 80% of industry revenue with new construction the remaining 20%; that supports cash-flow visibility and debt service in a downturn, but results are seasonal and the earnings history is not clean, because Beacon is in the figures from 29 April 2025, Kodiak from 1 April 2026 and TopBuild not at all. Customers are many and small, so credit exposure to any one account is low, and about 97% of net sales are in the United States.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C-25; calculation C-26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated: the founder held about 22.1% of voting power and his investment vehicle may designate 40% of the board while the 2024 investors keep at least 30% of fully diluted votes, figures stated as of the annual report and not updated for the 2026 issuances. The debt sits at the operating subsidiary, QXO Building Products, with Holdings pledging the borrower's equity and subsidiary guarantors behind each facility, while preferred and common equity are issued by QXO, Inc.; the filings do not say how cash reaches the parent to pay preferred dividends or whether the parent guarantees the debt. For creditors the points to monitor are the route of cash from the borrowing group to the parent and the restricted-payment limits, which the company calls not significant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume follows repair and re-roofing demand, housing starts and weather, so revenue is need-driven but not contractually recurring: the filings describe a transactional distribution model with volume rebates and give no contract duration or renewal data. Organic net sales were 1.56% below the pro forma prior year in the second quarter of 2026 and 5.05% below in the first half, so recent evidence is of falling volume or price rather than of durability, and the company attributes the result to current market conditions without separating volume from price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is partial. The company states that it has generally passed on manufacturers' price increases but that timing depends on competitive conditions, and gross margin fell in the second quarter as product cost rose faster than selling prices; customer concentration is low and supplier concentration high, so price discipline depends on the competitive pricing environment more than on switching costs, which the filings do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation C-07; calculation C-22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Selling, general and administrative expense was 20.0% of net sales in the second quarter of 2026 against 24.0% a year earlier, helped by lower stock-based compensation, restructuring and transaction costs than in the prior-year quarter, while the company states that many expenses are fixed. The first operational consequence is operating leverage in both directions: a fall in volume cuts gross profit with little cost relief, so repeating the first-half 2026 trends for twelve months would remove about USD 216 million of adjusted EBITDA, 29.79% of the pre-TopBuild base. Margin defence relies on price pass-through and on integration savings that the company does not quantify, and restructuring costs of USD 24 million and transformation costs of USD 36 million added back in the first half show that savings are still being paid for.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C-17; calculation C-28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was 1.14% of FY2025 net sales, so the model is asset-light and cash conversion is set by working capital, interest and acquisition costs rather than by capex. Free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months, 19.48% of adjusted EBITDA, before acquisitions and preferred dividends, and operating cash flow was negative in the first half of 2026 because receivables and inventories built ahead of the peak season; cash paid for income taxes was small at USD 5 million in the first half. Lease liabilities of USD 997 million sit outside the debt figures and about 97% of branches are leased, so occupancy cost is a fixed claim that competes with debt service in a downturn; EBITDA converts to free cash flow poorly today, and conversion falls further once run-rate interest and preferred dividends are counted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-05; calculation C-21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is meaningful but the industry is fragmented: the company describes thousands of small distributors alongside specialty distributors and big-box retailers competing on availability, technical advice, delivery, price and credit, and claims scale as the largest publicly traded roofing distributor. Scale helps purchasing and rebates, but the filings give no market-share, retention or entry-barrier data, so the strength of the moat is not established, and substitutes are not evidenced as a threat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is limited by customer fragmentation, since no customer exceeded 1% of net sales, although contractors can move volume on price. Supplier power is meaningful: three suppliers each supplied at least 10% of purchases and nearly 35% together, suppliers allocate product in shortages, and vendor rebates that lower cost can be changed; the effect lands on gross margin and fill rates rather than on solvency, but it is the force most likely to reach earnings quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C-22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and policy factors are material, and social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. Housing starts, business investment, interest rates and credit availability drive the new-construction and non-residential lines, and severe weather moves re-roofing demand in either direction; tariffs on steel and imported goods raise supplier prices and, if not passed on in time, margin. Higher interest rates also raise cost on floating debt: 42.38% of principal is floating after the incremental term loan and the supplied documents disclose no hedges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths in credit terms are scale across a broad contractor base, liquidity with no principal due before 2030, equity and preferred funding beneath the debt, and a capital-light model. Weaknesses are leverage that is not established after the closing, fixed charges of about USD 834 million at run rate, add-backs of 52.30% of adjusted EBITDA, falling organic sales and a seasonal cash trough.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-02; calculation C-06; calculation C-12; calculation C-15; calculation C-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are TopBuild earnings and integration savings that lower leverage, dividends on Series C stock paid in shares, and conversion of preferred stock that would end cash dividends. Threats that could weaken it are a soft housing or re-roofing season, tariff and asphalt cost shocks that are not passed on, a further debt-funded acquisition, failed integration of three businesses and higher rates on floating debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C-12; calculation C-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions the evidence supports the following assessments. Scale and market position are strong, with USD 9,898.2 million of twelve-month net sales and the largest publicly traded roofing distribution business in North America on the company's description. Competitive advantage is average, because scale supports purchasing but no market-share, retention or switching-cost data are supplied. Business diversification is average: customers are diversified and the mix is broadening, but nearly 35% of purchases come from three suppliers and about 97% of sales are in one country. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since capex is light but many expenses are fixed. Margin stability is weak, with adjusted gross margin down and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.38% against 10.70%. Free cash flow stability is weak, at 19.48% of adjusted EBITDA before preferred dividends. Ability to refinance is average, helped by no principal due before 2030 and by fair values of the notes above par at 30 June 2026, and held back by leverage that is not established. Liquidity position is strong at 30 June 2026, at USD 4,704 million, and not established after the closing. Financial policy and governance is average: equity funded the first two deals, but no leverage target is stated and control is concentrated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-04; calculation C-05; calculation C-15; calculation C-22; calculation C-25; calculation C-30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are liquidity, maturities and defensive demand, and the main constraints are fixed charges, earnings quality and the negative trend. The trend is deteriorating on organic sales and margin while debt rises, and the key missing datapoints are TopBuild's earnings, debt and cash, the margin on the incremental term loan and the first combined results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C-06; calculation C-07; calculation C-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the outlook turns on the first combined results for the quarter ending 30 September 2026, the first coupons on the 2031 and 2034 notes on 15 January 2027, which add to interest paid, and the first seasonal low with the enlarged charges. The company must show organic stabilisation and integration savings while restructuring and transformation costs are still being incurred, and the preferred stack adds about USD 264 million a year of dividends once Series C is fully issued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-12; calculation C-28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the management goal is to more than double EBITDA by 2030 and reach USD 50 billion of revenue within the decade, which is management language without a base year. The Series B preferred dividends end in May 2028, and USD 9,100 million of principal falls due between 2031 and 2034, USD 3,100 million of it on 30 April 2032, so refinancing is back-ended but concentrated. Sector tailwinds the company cites are a large housing shortage and an ageing housing stock that sustains repair demand; headwinds are the cyclicality of new construction, weather, tariffs and interest rates, and the company-specific headwinds are the integration of three businesses and the cost of the preferred stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C-18; calculation C-26; calculation C-29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside that fits this issuer is a repeat of first-half 2026 trading on the enlarged capital structure. The initiating condition is a soft housing and re-roofing season in the first quarter of 2027, the seasonal low, with organic volume falling again and selling prices lagging cost increases from asphalt, steel or tariffs. The first operational break is gross profit: repeating the 5.05% volume decline and a 1.0 percentage point margin loss for twelve months would remove about USD 216 million of adjusted EBITDA, 29.79% of the pre-TopBuild base, with little cost relief because many expenses are fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C-06; calculation C-07; calculation C-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission runs through fixed charges that do not flex: the first coupons on the 2031 and 2034 notes fall due on 15 January 2027, interest runs at about USD 570 million a year and preferred dividends at about USD 264 million, so a seasonal half year at those charges would use about USD 511 million of cash, covered 9.20x by total liquidity of USD 4,704 million. Leverage is the casualty rather than liquidity: lower earnings against the added debt would push leverage above where it would otherwise be, by an amount that cannot be quantified because TopBuild's earnings are not supplied, and the 2031 to 2034 maturities of USD 9,100 million would then be refinanced from a weaker position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-09; calculation C-12; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are real but limited: Series C dividends of USD 142.5 million can be paid in shares, there is no common dividend, capital expenditure is only 1.14% of net sales and so offers little, and ABL availability of USD 1,930 million and a history of raising equity are the main backstops. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within the next 12 months, as the company also states, but not sufficient to show deleveraging. Primary downside path: a weak first quarter of 2027 on top of the first full burden of new interest and preferred dividends, before TopBuild's earnings are shown to carry them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 62; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-05; calculation C-12; calculation C-14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, QXO presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, defensive demand, low customer concentration and liquidity of USD 4,704 million, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that cannot be established after the TopBuild closing, add-backs of 52.30% of adjusted EBITDA, falling organic sales and run-rate fixed charges of about USD 834 million. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was USD 141.2 million over twelve months before acquisitions and preferred dividends and is negative in the first half. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on TopBuild's earnings, on the seasonal pattern and on whether acquisitions are held to what equity can fund; no principal falls due before 2030. The primary downside path is a weak first quarter of 2027 on the enlarged charges. Further analysis would require TopBuild's earnings, debt and cash, the margin on the incremental term loan and the first combined results. Top risk: leverage and fixed charges after the TopBuild closing, which no supplied document measures.
